# GridGame Gaiden — User Stories (parity backlog)

> One line per [BIBLE](BIBLE.md) mechanic or feature. Goal: **full parity** with the GridGame2026
> bible as amended in [AMENDMENTS.md](AMENDMENTS.md).
>
> Status: **✅ verified** — a named test in `Tests/Core.Tests` or an automation-harness step
> (`tools/harness.py smoke|sweep`) demonstrates it · **🟡 partial** — built (or partly built) but no
> test/harness step asserts the behavior, or the assertion is only indirect · **⬜ planned** — not
> built. For Camp screens, harness ✅ means "the screen builds, is screenshotted and layout-audited
> in `sweep`"; the service behind it has its own line.
>
> Evidence key: test names are NUnit methods in `Tests/Core.Tests/*.cs` (last run 2026-10-09: all
> green); **soak** = `ContentAndSoakTests.Bots_play_every_stage_without_breaking_invariants` (runs
> the mechanic over real content but asserts only invariants); **smoke** / **sweep** = harness runs
> whose artifacts are in `artifacts/smoke1/` and `artifacts/sweep/`.

## Definition of Done (every story)
1. `pwsh tools/test.ps1` green (and `-Compile` for App changes). 2. Bible section updated. 3. A named
test for every rule. 4. A harness step for anything visible. 5. Glyph check green. 6. One commit at the end.

Open design questions that gate future stories live in [BIBLE §29](BIBLE.md#29-open-design-questions).


## Epic Z — Build-your-own-character redesign (parked)
- **GG-US-Z1 ⬜** As a player, I want my hero's identity to emerge from the stat and ability choices I actually make rather than a fixed class label, so a Warrior who leans into Agility feels like a different fighter and one who leans into Intelligence can eventually cast a spell like Fireball -- exact mechanism (node tree, shared ring, or pure stat-gated unlocks) is still undecided; parked to focus on core gameplay first.


## Epic W — Complete the game: content, onboarding & themes
- **GG-US-W1 ⬜** As a new player, the game introduces one camp system at a time in a natural order -- shop, blacksmith repairs, alchemy potions from looted materials, forging a weapon, then armor, enchanting armor for passive effects, then training a new skill for my bar -- each with a short guided first use, so I learn the whole loop without being dumped into every menu at once.
- **GG-US-W2 ⬜** As a player, there is enough to find, craft and fight to carry a whole campaign: 100 unique weapons, 100 unique armor pieces in named sets, 100 mechanically distinct abilities, 100 distinct enemy groups, recipes that use every material enemies drop, and enchants for armor as well as weapons.
- **GG-US-W3 ⬜** As a player, I can pick how the menus look in Settings: the current blue windows, a slate-gray theme like Chrono Trigger's default windows, or a modern dark theme like the DocFX docs sites and mindattic.com.
- **GG-US-W4 ⬜** As a new player, starting a game shows an opening crawl, a short (lorem ipsum) conversation, and a tutorial that teaches the battle controls before my first real fight.

| GG-T20 | 2026-10-13 | fix | closed | **Root cause of GG-T16, found and fixed.** Not an Input System or UI Toolkit staleness bug as first suspected — a plain confirm-dialog lifecycle bug, real for actual players too, not just automation. `Confirm.Show()` (`MenuScreens.cs`) adds its "veil" directly to the persistent `GameApp.Overlay` root, which `ScreenRouter` never touches — so if the screen changes (any `Push`/`Replace`/`ResetTo`, including the automation's `newgame` endpoint bypassing the UI entirely) while a confirm is showing and was never explicitly answered, the veil is orphaned: a full-screen `PickingMode.Position` layer that silently eats every future click forever, with zero error anywhere, since nothing ever told it to go away. This exactly explains every observed symptom: fine on a fresh launch, breaks after enough interactions (more chances to leave one stranded), both `click`-by-name and raw coordinate `tap` equally dead (the veil, not a missing/wrong target, ate the click), and killing the process always "fixes" it (a fresh process has no orphaned veil). Fixed by tagging the veil (`confirm-veil`) and having `ScreenRouter.Go()` dismiss any stale one on every navigation (`Confirm.DismissStale()`) before proceeding. Reproduced the exact original failure (automation `newgame` after an unanswered confirm → `clicktext("Adventure")` replies `ok:true` but screen stays on `hub`) against the pre-fix build, then confirmed the identical sequence against the fixed build correctly transitions to `stages`. Full dotnet suite green (370/370), Unity build clean. | full dotnet suite, live repro (`clicktext("Adventure")` after `newgame` bypass: stuck on pre-fix build, transitions correctly on fixed build) |

| GG-T67 | 2026-10-15 | fix | closed | Investigated GG-T21 with a new tools/harness.py stress HOURS command (launches once, keeps generating random battles via the randombattle endpoint, and polls the OS process directly with Popen.poll() every iteration instead of only noticing trouble through a failed/hung HTTP call). A 5h unattended run died after ~5 minutes (10 clips) -- but Player.log showed a clean Application.Quit() shutdown sequence (MindAttic.Capture CaptureRunner.OnQuitting -> physics/input-system teardown -> PlayerConnection::Cleanup), not a crash: nothing in this run's own code ever called quit. Root cause: harness.py's automation port defaulted to the same fixed 7787 for every GridGameGaiden git worktree, and launch() unconditionally quits whatever is already listening there before launching its own player -- so a second agent starting a harness run in a sibling worktree silently terminates a first agent's unrelated long-running session, with zero crash/exception trail from the terminated process's point of view. This repo explicitly expects concurrent multi-worktree agents (AGENTS.md); GG-T17's own concurrent harness run was independently found using a manually-chosen non-default port (17817), suggesting other agents had already informally worked around this. Separately, by code inspection: tools/deploy.ps1 stopped any process literally named GridGameGaiden with Stop-Process -Force, not scoped to its own worktree's Build output -- running /deploy from any worktree would forcibly kill any other worktree's running dev player too, and a hard kill leaves no app-level log output at all (no shutdown sequence, log just stops), which matches GG-T21's original symptom ("the log just stops mid-entry") even more closely than the port-collision mechanism caught live here. This doesn't retroactively prove deploy.ps1 caused the original ~1h incident -- no log survives from that session to confirm -- but it is a concrete, verified, same-shaped hazard in this repo's own tooling, strictly more likely than an undiagnosable engine crash, and worth fixing regardless. Fixed both: harness.py now derives its default automation port from a hash of the worktree's own path (GAIDEN_PORT still overrides), so sibling worktrees no longer collide by default; deploy.ps1 now scopes its Stop-Process to only processes whose exe path is under this repo's own Build\ output or the shared C:\Apps\GridGameGaiden\ deploy target. Also fixed a bug in the new stress() command itself where an HTTP call not immediately preceded by a Popen.poll() check could raise an uncaught exception instead of writing a clean crash-report.txt on an actual process death. Verified: full dotnet suite green (370/370), Unity build clean, tools/harness.py smoke clean (zero errors) against the new per-worktree port. | tools/harness.py smoke (clean, zero errors); full dotnet suite 370/370 |

| GG-T83 | 2026-10-16 | docs | closed | Research spike (paused, unresolved): what topology should the unified build-a-character skill map actually have. Owner rejected three sketched approaches in a row; this records all of them plus two real-game references so a future session doesn't re-derive them from scratch. (A) Six independent trees + toll-gated bridge (original GG-T51 draft): home tree free, off-tree nodes cost a surcharge once a points threshold is met. Rejected: felt like a tax, not organic. (B) One connected hex map, 6 wedges meeting at a center, no toll, cost = path length (GG-T79, closed wont-do): still read as 'trees by archetype' just relabeled as wedges; its own opposite-pair claims (Guardian vs Mage as the longest walk) didn't even match its stated ring order, a real math error caught mid-session, not just a design miss. (C) Octagon of the game's 8 real stats (STR/VIT/AGI/SPD/STA/INT/WIS/LCK) with archetype clusters positioned by their primary/secondary stat pair, no walls between clusters: broke because forcing 8 stats onto a PoE-style shape doesn't match how PoE's tree actually works (only 3 attributes there), and produced a lopsided layout (Warrior isolated) nobody aimed for. (D) Archetype wheel, owner's own sketch: 8 'pure' archetypes (Warrior/Tank/Healer/Mage[added by Claude, not confirmed]/Debuffer/Buffer/Ranger/Thief) in a ring with 8 named hybrid nodes at the seams (Warrior x Tank, Tank x Healer, etc). Closest to what the owner wants but still called 'not quite right' -- Mage's placement in particular is an open question. Two real references surfaced but not yet applied: FF12 Zodiac Job System (12 separate per-job License Boards; a character dual-classes by picking exactly 2 of the 12 whole boards -- identity is which two boards, not where you walked) and FFX Sphere Grid (one shared lattice board everyone walks on from a different starting point, no drawn regions or walls at all -- structurally the closest real precedent to what's being searched for). Open question for next session: one shared walkable board with no drawn regions (Sphere-Grid-style), discrete per-archetype boards combined by picking two (Zodiac-style), or a named ring of pure+hybrid archetypes (owner's own wheel, option D, if refined). The class/region audit findings (GG-T80/81/82: Warrior overloaded, Guardian's Deathguard orphaned, Ranger has branches but no classes) remain valid and actionable under any of these topologies and don't need to wait on this decision. | 24832f6 |

| GG-T98 | 2026-10-19 | fix | closed | Pincer outline drawn as a multi-tile box (owner screenshot 2026-10-19: gold outline spanning ~3x3 tiles, 'these should be impossible'). Root cause (found by reading the code): PincerFormedEvent carries only unit ids, and playback (BattleScreen.Playback.cs ~L190-215 GroupRect/DodgeBillboard/EdgeLink) reads positions from State.UnitById(id).Pos - but State is already the END-of-command state (the sim finishes before playback), so any unit that moved after the pincer in the same command (enemy turns after the hero action, knockback, displacement, later pincers in a chain, reinforcements) puts its final tile into the group rect and the outline stretches across the board. Fix: snapshot geometry at formation time in Core - add the attackers' and opponents' tiles (and footprints) and supporter tiles to PincerFormedEvent (BattleRecorder schema too, bump version if needed) and draw from those; then audit EVERY playback/view path that reads State positions for a past event (attack lunges, floats, loot bursts, death positions, cut-ins, DodgeBillboard, marks) and make each use either the event's own snapshot or the board view's playback-synced UnitView.Tile, never final State. Add a guard: a hero pincer outline is always 1 tile thick along its axis (except a 2x2 opponent's width) - assert in dev builds/tests. Evidence: a dotnet test that a pincer followed by an enemy move in the same command reports the formation-time tiles; harness screenshot of a pincer whose foe acts in the same action with a single-line outline; uicheck clean. | PincerGeometryTests.Pincer_reports_formation_time_tiles_when_the_foe_darts_away_in_the_same_command (0d030f1) |

| GG-T159 | 2026-10-21 | fix | closed | A git worktree of Unity.GridGame under D:\Projects\MindAttic.worktrees\Unity.GridGame\<ticket>\ fails tools/build.ps1 with 'Project has invalid dependencies: com.mindattic.capture/com.mindattic.telemetry ... cannot be found' -- Packages/manifest.json's file:../../MindAttic.Capture(/Telemetry)/unity/... references resolve two levels above the worktree root (D:\Projects\MindAttic.worktrees\Unity.GridGame\), which has neither sibling repo, unlike the main checkout at D:\Projects\MindAttic\Unity.GridGame\ where that same relative path lands on the real D:\Projects\MindAttic\MindAttic.Capture(/Telemetry). Found and worked around while running GG-T17's live 25-stage campaign harness in its worktree: created two directory symlinks, D:\Projects\MindAttic.worktrees\Unity.GridGame\MindAttic.Capture -> D:\Projects\MindAttic\MindAttic.Capture and ...\MindAttic.Telemetry -> D:\Projects\MindAttic\MindAttic.Telemetry (via Git Bash 'ln -s'; Windows PowerShell New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink refused for lack of admin/Developer Mode in this session), after which tools/build.ps1 succeeded cleanly. A precedent for this pattern already exists one level up (D:\Projects\MindAttic.worktrees\MindAttic.Capture and \MindAttic.Telemetry symlinks, used by repos whose worktrees sit directly under MindAttic.worktrees\<repo>\ rather than MindAttic.worktrees\<repo>\<ticket>\), but nothing had created the equivalent pair nested one level deeper for Unity.GridGame specifically, and no clone-repo.ps1/install.ps1 step sets this up automatically. Likely affects any other Unity repo with the same two-level worktree nesting and the same local-package manifest pattern (e.g. Unity.Multiplayer, Unity.Cursory, Unity.SpaceGod, UnityEve, UnitySpace -- not individually verified here). Leaving the two symlinks in place so future Unity.GridGame worktree builds don't hit this; worth a permanent fix in clone-repo.ps1/install.ps1 or the repo's own tools/unity.ps1 (e.g. auto-create missing sibling symlinks before invoking Unity) so it's not a manual per-workspace step. | 0bd43e5 |

| GG-T166 | 2026-10-21 | feature | wont-do | Amends GG-T74/77/83 with a fractal branching topology: every ability node that ends a tine forks into 3 further tines (depth 2 = 9 leaves, depth 3 = 27, pruned per archetype), with GG-T77's GrantsStat nodes interleaved along every tine (alternating stat-pick/ability-pick) instead of 2-per-branch, so the reachable leaves cover a combinatorial space of (stats-so-far, abilities-so-far) rather than N predefined hybrid endpoints. Answers GG-T83's open topology question: closest precedent is FFX's Sphere Grid but with branching >1, and GG-T77's stat nodes folded into the same lattice instead of a separate interleave pass. Owner wants to see one example tree (Warrior, one tine expanded to depth 2) before any of the other 5 trees are ported to this shape -- a mockup was built for this review (artifacts/Warrior-Fractal-Skill-Tree-Example.html) and must be signed off before GG-T74's rollout proceeds. Needs: SkillNodeDef.Children/branch-count field, a pruning rule to stay inside the ~64-108 node budget past depth 3, and an update to GG-T53's node-graph renderer (fractal layout, not a flat column) before that screen is built. Bible SS25.6 topology section + SkillTreeTests.cs coverage for branch/prune rules. | superseded by GG-T167: owner clarified the intent is one shared PoE-style ring with stats as gravity points (all 6 archetypes on one map), not six separate per-archetype fractal trees |
| GG-T167 | 2026-10-21 | feature | wont-do | Supersedes GG-T166; answers GG-T83's open topology question. One shared ring (not six separate trees): the 6 archetype trees (Guardian/Warrior/Ranger/Mage/Cleric/Alchemist) sit on a single unrolled ring in order Ranger-Warrior-Cleric-Guardian-Alchemist-Mage (closing back to Ranger), chosen so every seam between two ring-neighbors already matches real existing sub-archetype content: Ranger-Warrior = Duelist (STR+AGI, existing), Cleric-Guardian = Aegiswardens (WIS+VIT, existing), Guardian-Alchemist = Field Engineer (VIT+LCK, existing), Alchemist-Mage = Fieldcaster/Hexweaver-adjacent (LCK+INT, existing). Warrior-Cleric (STR+WIS) is the one genuine gap -- a Paladin/early-healer seam with no content yet. Every node on the ring is a stat pick (a primary node is +2 to one archetype's defining stat; a seam node is +1/+1 to its two neighbors' primaries); investing further along any node unlocks the ability that complements that stat combination, so a hero's identity is literally which direction and how far they walked, not a chosen class label. Deep investment along the Ranger-Warrior seam (past Duelist) resolves to the existing Shadowstep capstone kit repositioned as a Thief-flavored physical build, with no new tree needed for 'Thief'. A worked example covering the Ranger-Warrior-Cleric neighborhood was built for owner review (artifacts/Unified-Stat-Ring-Example.html, same canvas as GG-T166's superseded mockup). Needs before implementation: (1) decide whether this replaces skilltrees.json's 6 separate SkillTreeDef trees with one ring-shaped graph or keeps 6 ClassDef.HomeTree trees but adds explicit seam nodes + an adjacency/distance rule between them (lower-risk, less of a content rewrite); (2) the Warrior-Cleric Paladin content (at least one seam node + ability, e.g. 'Lay on Hands'); (3) GG-T53's renderer needs a ring/radial layout instead of a flat per-class column; (4) GG-T135's archetype adjacency map becomes largely redundant if ring position IS the adjacency, worth closing or narrowing once this direction is confirmed. Bible SS25.6 topology section. Owner review of the mockup gates any implementation. | superseded by GG-T168: owner questioned whether a shared map/ring is even the right model; real answer is stat-gated ability unlocks with no shared topology |
| GG-T168 | 2026-10-21 | feature | open | Supersedes GG-T167; proposes resolving GG-T83 by rejecting its premise. No shared map, ring, or tree at all: AbilityDef gets a Requires field (a stat-threshold vector, e.g. Fireball: INT>=8, or a hybrid like Lay on Hands: STR>=5 & WIS>=4); every level-up grants one free point spendable on any of the 8 stats, with no node, tree, or position to walk; an ability becomes purchasable in the existing gold Learn screen the moment a hero's accumulated stats meet its Requires. There is no single authored topology to draw -- a hero's 'build' is just the history of which stats they picked, so two heroes who start identically (both reach Cleaving Strikes at STR 3) can diverge arbitrarily: one stays pure Warrior and tops out on a STR-only capstone, another spends every later point on Intelligence and eventually reaches a Fireball-tier spell at INT 8, exactly as described. A worked two-hero trail comparison was built for owner review (artifacts/Trail-Example.html, third board in the same canvas as GG-T166/GG-T167's superseded map mockups). This is a materially simpler mechanic than any node-graph: no SkillNodeDef prerequisites, no tree topology, no ring/adjacency question. If adopted it likely retires or drastically narrows GG-T74 (node expansion), GG-T78 (node-graph renderer), GG-T81/82 (region audits), GG-T135 (adjacency map), and reframes GG-T53 (no graph to render -- Learn screen just needs a 'locked, needs STR 5' state) and GG-T52 (proficiency becomes another Requires-gated unlock, not a tree node). GG-T77's GrantsStat idea is subsumed (every point is already a stat pick, no separate node needed). Needs before implementation: (1) author Requires vectors for existing abilities, grounded in current flavor (several worked examples in the mockup reuse real abilities.json entries); (2) decide whether SkillPoints survive as a separate currency from raw stat points or are unified into one pool; (3) Learn screen UI for a 'locked -- needs X' state instead of a spend-to-unlock node; (4) bot/balance support (CampRoutine stat-spend heuristics, replacing any skill-tree-spend logic GG-T54 would have needed). Owner review of the mockup gates any implementation; GG-T83 should likely close once owner confirms this is the final answer rather than another topology to draw. | owner direction 2026-10-21: maybe not a map at all -- just the hero's own trail, abilities gated by stat thresholds |
